key_insight: Adjoint sensitivity maps show where local passive flow-control around rotating cylinders can simultaneously reduce drag and lift, with the dominant field structure set mainly by spinning ratio rather than Reynolds number.
engineering_relevance: The sensitivity atlas offers a practical design guide for placing passive devices near Flettner rotors and other rotating cylinders to improve aerodynamic performance over broad operating conditions.
method: Topology-based adjoint sensitivity analysis over Re = 1e1 to 1e7 and spinning ratios 0 to 2π
Porous-medium formulation to compute local sensitivity fields for drag, lift, and torque
Validation with forward simulations using distributed Darcy-type sources and a sensitivity-informed passive control structure
evidence_signal: The abstract reports dedicated forward-simulation validation and a systematic scan of the operating envelope, showing the sensitivity-field topology is largely governed by spinning ratio with comparatively weak Reynolds-number effects.
watch_item: The maps guide passive-device placement, but performance remains contingent on how well the porous-medium sensitivity model and the real control geometry match the actual flow configuration.
paper_title: Adjoint Sensitivity Maps for Passive Flow Control Around Rotating Circular Cylinders Across a Wide Operating Envelope
